newsitem.title: UK: UK bank stocks soar higher, HSBC up 4.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: UK bank stocks soar higher, HSBC up 4.6 pct.

text.p: Shares in British banks soared yet higher amid a massive squeeze in the market overall, dealers and analysts said.

"There's no one big issue. They've been pushed by people trying to up their weightings with the building societies floating. They're having their traditional outperformance ahead of results and the results will be solid with strong dividend growth," said one analyst.
The sector's reporting season comes in early August.
"Also sterling strength is helping with the banks' big domestic exposure," he said.
HSBC Holdings Plc surged 95-1/2p to 2,181-1/2p, National Westminster Bank Plc 20p to 873p, Lloyds TSB Group Plc 16-1/2p to 714p and Barclays Bank Plc 31-1/2p to 1,284p.
The sector continued to benefit from Dresdner Kleinwort Benson raising its target share price on Tuesday for HSBC to 2,400p from 2,100p and for Lloyds to 830p from 780p, dealers said.
Dresdner Kleinwort repeated its negative stance on NatWest which today said its investment banking arm had not yet completed its review of operations.
